# docs_audit_report — 2026-06-15

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero is genuinely strong — I know what Carnot does in one line and how to
install it. But the moment I scroll, the page turns on itself: the very first
"headline" card admits a previous number was wrong ("Repinned from v2 0.9857"),
the Evidence section is a 12-card wall of unexplained acronyms (FoVer,
EstimationVerifier, SVAMP, VeriCoT, PRM-BiasBench, HalluGuard v3, CCTU, CRANE),
and several results are suspiciously perfect (1.0, 60/60, 99.3%) sitting right
next to a defensive paragraph about "synthetic pilots." Net: I'd read the hero,
get uneasy at the Evidence section, and likely close the tab before the
preprint. The page argues with itself instead of selling.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. Trust-eroding "internal laundry" in the very first card — the hero stats-bar
   "Recent progress" card volunteers "Repinned from v2 0.9857 after
   pre-submission adversarial audit." A stranger reads: "they previously
   published a number that was wrong, by a lot." That belongs in a blog post,
   not the headline.
2. The Evidence section is insider-only — 12 cards, most headlined by an
   acronym a stranger has never seen, with no one-line glosses. A stranger
   skims none of them and learns nothing.
3. Numbers that look too good with no credibility anchor — TP rate 0.5→1.0,
   "60/60 attacks," "99.3% flagged," "identical losses." On a page that ALSO
   contains a defensive disclaimer about provenance and a "we had to retract a
   number" admission, the perfect scores read as cooked, not impressive.

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- Note: the page is reasonably tight on raw word count — no bento body exceeds
  ~120 words and no footer/card body breaks the caps. The damage here is card
  COUNT and density, not length:
- Evidence / results-grid — 12 cards — a stranger skims none; cut to the 4–6
  strongest, plainly-labeled wins. (Soft cap ~6–8 for a landing page.)
- Whole-page card load — ~32 cards total (2 problem + 11 bento + 12 results + 7
  blog) — heavy scroll. The Evidence block is the worst offender.
- Hero stats-bar "Recent progress" r-card (~55 words) — fine on length, but it
  is crammed INTO the four headline stats, mixing a prose paragraph into what
  should be four clean numbers. Visually muddies the strongest real estate.

### Inconsistencies
- AUROC numbers collide: stats-bar says 0.9131 (FoVer); the hero card says

- FoVer is simultaneously the project's flagship strength (0.9131 AUROC,
  headline stat) AND a weak baseline being beaten ("0.90 AUC vs 0.125 FoVer

- "Seven capabilities, one framework" — there are 7 feature cards, but 2 of

### Fabrication signals
- "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" (Evidence) — a perfect 1.0 with no
  sample size shown.
- "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" (Evidence) — perfect score, tiny n=60,

- "99.3% of wrong code flagged" (Code bento) — suspiciously precise/high on a
  164-problem set.
- "2.0× speedup, identical losses" (Evidence) — "identical" is an absolute
  claim begging for an asterisk.
- Multiple 100%-width meter bars (FPGA, training, fuzzing, TP-rate, 60/60)

- Aggravating context: these perfect numbers sit next to a "we had to retract
  0.9857" admission and a provenance disclaimer — so instead of impressing, the
